solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drained of colour, suddenly (3,2,3,4)

blocks.note: read literally: with the blue taken out
the everyday idiom for without warning

annotation.surface: Something goes pale all at once, like a face losing its colour in shock.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the phrase: whatever has had the blue drained away is out of the blue.
annotation.definitionFit: Out of the blue means unexpectedly, which is what suddenly means.

entries.clue: Test going round part – of the M25? (7)

indicatorNotes.going round: ORAL goes round the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam

annotation.surface: An exam going round part of London's great ring road, as if the test were a traffic survey.
annotation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway ringing London, known as the London Orbital; the question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: The M25 circles London, so something of the M25 is orbital, running in a ring.

entries.clue: Evidently sore after hit on the bottom, one whacked (5)

indicatorNotes.on the bottom: the bottom of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.after: RED comes after the other pieces

annotation.surface: Someone smacked on the backside is visibly sore afterwards.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a spanking, but whacked here is the British slang for exhausted, and hit and bottom are there only to supply one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Whacked is British slang for worn out, i.e. tired.

entries.clue: Money about right, weapon for charger without contract (9)

indicatorNotes.about: FEE goes about R, surrounding it

blocks.note: a knight's weapon when charging on horseback

annotation.surface: A mercenary knight weighs up his pay and his lance while riding without any contract.
annotation.walkthrough: The word freelance began as a mercenary knight, a lance free to hire, so the surface's charger is historically apt.
annotation.definitionFit: A freelance works for many clients without a permanent employment contract.

entries.clue: Cover carpet, surface unseen (4)

indicatorNotes.surface unseen: the top (surface) letter of a down answer is not shown

blocks.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them

annotation.surface: Laying a carpet so the floor beneath can no longer be seen.
annotation.walkthrough: Carpet looks like a noun for flooring, but it is the verb to carpet, meaning to tell someone off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to put something out of sight under a blanket or lid is both to cover and to hide it.

entries.clue: Singer, Scot for example, entertaining American individual (8)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: to entertain a guest is to hold them within

blocks.note: a Scot is one kind of Brit

annotation.surface: A Scottish singer hosts a visiting American.
annotation.walkthrough: Singer in the surface names a performer, and it is simply the definition; the Scot is only there to be a Brit.
annotation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singer with a voice between tenor and bass.

entries.clue: Your bank’s shut in town (5)

annotation.definitionNote: town is used as a modifier (town planning), matching the adjective urban

indicatorNotes.shut in: the answer is enclosed within the words before it

annotation.surface: Your bank branch has closed its doors in town.
annotation.walkthrough: Shut in reads like a closed-down branch; here it tells you the answer is shut inside the other words.
annotation.definitionFit: Town used as a modifier, as in town life or town planning, carries the same sense as the Latin-derived adjective for built-up places.

entries.clue: Englishman abroad with queen, one’s scented (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a phrase standing for a noun: one (a thing) that is scented

blocks.note: Australian slang for an English person

annotation.surface: An English traveller and a queen, one of whom wears perfume.
annotation.walkthrough: Abroad points to how Australians and New Zealanders call the English Poms.
annotation.definitionFit: A pomander is a ball of perfumed substances, a thing that is scented.

entries.clue: Loom I fix that conserves power (6)

indicatorNotes.that conserves: MEND keeps P safe inside itself

annotation.surface: A weaver repairs a loom in an energy-saving way.
annotation.walkthrough: Loom sits first as a noun for a weaving frame, but it is the verb, to hang over threateningly.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that impends looms, threatening to happen soon.

entries.clue: Halt in trade for landlord, say (9)

blocks.note: legal tender is what is accepted in trade

annotation.surface: A publican is ordered to stop dealing.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage a landlord is also the keeper of a pub, and the say marks him as an example of someone serving drinks.
annotation.definitionFit: A pub landlord pours the drinks, so he is one example of a bartender.

entries.clue: Report about opening of leaf in flower (5)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' in its sense of around, so the report's letters stand around the L
indicatorNotes.opening of: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a report is a loud bang

annotation.surface: A news report about a leaf unfurling in a flower.
annotation.walkthrough: Report is a gunshot-style bang, not a news story.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: gardeners speak of a single bloom on a rose bush just as they would of a flower.

entries.clue: Little worse for wear (6)

annotation.surface: Someone is a bit the worse for wear.
annotation.walkthrough: Read together, the clue says slightly drunk, which is itself the second sense; tiddly is British slang both for tiny and for a bit tipsy.
annotation.definitionFit: Tiddly means very small, and also mildly drunk.

entries.clue: Neanderthal figure breaks leg (5-3)

indicatorNotes.breaks: ONE breaks into STAGE, splitting it

blocks.note: a leg of a journey is a stage

annotation.surface: A caveman figure snaps his leg.
annotation.walkthrough: Figure looks like a body, but it is a number.
annotation.definitionFit: Neanderthal, used as an adjective for something primitive, means stone-age.

entries.clue: Regret seeing people from Los Angeles ending in Pontefract (6)

indicatorNotes.ending in: the end letter of the word that follows

annotation.surface: Californians rue their journey finishing in a Yorkshire town.
annotation.walkthrough: Pontefract is a small town in Yorkshire, England, a comic comedown from Los Angeles.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to express sorrow over something past is both to regret and to lament it.

entries.clue: Bone thrown in heap on the way out (8)

indicatorNotes.thrown in: something thrown in lands inside the heap, so the bone ends up enclosed by it

annotation.surface: A bone tossed on the pile as it leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: Bone and heap together suggest a graveyard, which suits a word meaning dying.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: on the way out describes anything close to death or obsolescence, which is the Latin-rooted word's sense of dying.

entries.clue: Fixed indeed, so probably a foregone conclusion? (3-5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a noun phrase describing a contest; the answer is the adjective for such a contest

indicatorNotes.Fixed: fixing rearranges things, as a rigged result is fixed

annotation.surface: A match that was rigged is naturally a foregone conclusion.
annotation.walkthrough: The so looks like part of the fodder's sentence, and it is: both indeed and so are rearranged. A one-sided contest has an outcome known in advance.
annotation.definitionFit: A one-sided contest is so unequal that its result is all but certain.

entries.clue: Bad taste, pig stuffed with hot Italian food (9)

indicatorNotes.Bad: a bad version is a mangled one
indicatorNotes.stuffed with: the rearranged letters are filled with H

annotation.surface: A nasty-tasting pig stuffed with spicy Italian food.
annotation.walkthrough: Stuffed with suggests a roast pig with a filling; here the jumbled letters of taste and pig are the thing stuffed, and H goes in.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the long thin pasta strands are among the best-known dishes of Italy.

entries.clue: Piper cares to play organ (8)

indicatorNotes.to play: the letters play about into a new order

blocks.note: Pan, the Greek god who plays pipes

annotation.surface: A musician on pipes wants to play the church organ.
annotation.walkthrough: Organ looks like the instrument, keeping the music going, but it is a body part.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the gland behind the stomach that makes insulin and digestive juices is one of the body's organs.

entries.clue: Rider Haggard’s first novel a sermon (8)

indicatorNotes.novel: novel as in new, making the letters new

annotation.surface: H. Rider Haggard's debut book was a sermon.
annotation.walkthrough: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines, and the surface splits his name so Rider is the definition. Novel looks like a book but means new.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone on horseback is a rider, the surface's first name for Haggard doing double duty.

entries.clue: Plague in shelter regularly, donkey quarantined (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so only letters spaced evenly through the word are kept
indicatorNotes.quarantined: ASS is shut away inside the other letters

annotation.surface: An animal is kept isolated in a shelter during a plague outbreak.
annotation.walkthrough: Plague looks like the disease that makes quarantine necessary, but it is the verb, to pester.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to keep bothering someone is to plague them, the informal word being the modern equivalent.

entries.clue: Blight on rank vegetable (6)

indicatorNotes.on: one piece is placed on the next in the across entry

annotation.surface: Disease strikes a foul-smelling vegetable.
annotation.walkthrough: Blight and rank both suggest rot in the garden; they are the verb to spoil and a line of things. A marrow is a large squash grown in British gardens.
annotation.definitionFit: A marrow is a large vegetable of the squash family.

entries.clue: Thingummy that now needs repairing (7)

indicatorNotes.needs repairing: the letters must be put together again

annotation.surface: Some gadget whose name escapes you is now broken.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is the everyday frustration of a broken thing you cannot name, and the answer is one of the words for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A whatnot, like a thingummy, is a word for something whose name you cannot recall.

entries.clue: Take time with two vehicles reversing (8)

annotation.surface: Take your time while two cars are backing up.
annotation.walkthrough: Take is the arithmetic sense, as in take four from ten.
annotation.definitionFit: The arithmetic sense: in take four from ten, take means to remove one number from another.

entries.clue: Roof blown off farmhouse, sweep (5)

indicatorNotes.Roof blown off: the top letter of a down answer is removed

blocks.note: a grange is a farmhouse with outbuildings

annotation.surface: A storm tears the roof from a farmhouse and a sweep follows.
annotation.walkthrough: Sweep looks like chimney cleaning after the roof goes, but it is a noun for extent.
annotation.definitionFit: A range is the full sweep or extent of something.

entries.clue: Dread playing hit, ostensibly Brothers in Arms, first of all (6)

indicatorNotes.first of all: the first letter of each word

blocks.clueFragment: playing hit, ostensibly Brothers in Arms
blocks.note: Playing Hit Ostensibly Brothers In Arms

annotation.surface: Someone dreads hearing Dire Straits' big hit played again.
annotation.walkthrough: Brothers in Arms is a 1985 Dire Straits album and song, which is why ostensibly and hit are there.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an irrational, overwhelming fear of something, such as spiders or heights, is a dread.

entries.clue: Brightness initially with shortage in dark (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so only the word's first letter is used

annotation.surface: A shortage of light leaves things dark.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a description of the answer: brightness in short supply leaves black.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a night with no light at all is dark, or at its extreme, pitch black.

entries.clue: Embroidered, fake news (4)

indicatorNotes.fake: a fake is a false version, the letters rearranged

annotation.surface: A story has been embellished, making it fake news.
annotation.walkthrough: Embroidered in the surface means exaggerated, as in an embroidered tale; the answer takes it literally, as needlework.
annotation.definitionFit: The literal needlework sense: decoration stitched onto cloth with thread has been embroidered, i.e. worked with a needle.

entries.clue: Stripe on new pillowcases etc (5)

indicatorNotes.on: LINE is placed on N in the across entry

annotation.surface: A stripe printed on new pillowcases.
annotation.walkthrough: Linen here is household bedding in general, not only the fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: Pillowcases, sheets and the like are bed linen.

entries.clue: Try and see in when blurry, nursing a pain from looking? (9)

indicatorNotes.nursing: the jumbled letters hold A as a nurse holds a baby

annotation.surface: Squinting to see when your vision is blurry gives you a pain from looking.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes eyestrain, and its a is shared: a letter in the wordplay and the article of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is the ache that comes from overworking the eyes.

entries.clue: Ice skates not designed for series of passes (6,6)

indicatorNotes.designed: the letters are designed into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Skates unsuited to a run of passing moves, as in ice hockey.
annotation.walkthrough: NOT is part of the fodder and designed alone is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A season ticket covers a whole series of admissions or journeys.
